Corollary 771Sections pull back injectively over every open

Let \(T\) be an object of \(\mathrm{Over}(\operatorname{Spec}k)\) and \(W \subseteq T\) any open. Then pullback of sections along the second projection, \(\Gamma (T, W) \to \Gamma (C \otimes T, \mathrm{pr}^{-1}W)\), is injective.

Corollary 766Triviality is detected on the representing cover

For a pointed cover \(\mathcal U\) of a scheme \(X\) and \(a \in \check H^1(\mathcal U)\), the Picard class \([\mathcal U, a] \in \operatorname{Pic}(X)\) is trivial if and only if \(a = 1\).

LaTeX Lean
Corollary 767\(\check H^1\) of a cover embeds in the Picard group

For every pointed cover \(\mathcal U\) of a scheme \(X\), the canonical map \(\check H^1(\mathcal U) \to \operatorname{Pic}(X)\), \(a \mapsto [\mathcal U, a]\), is injective.

LaTeX Lean
Corollary 688Morphisms with one-point range kill Čech classes

Let \(K\) be a field, \(D, E\) objects of \(\mathrm{Over}(\operatorname{Spec}K)\) with \(D\) reduced, and \(h : D \to E\) a morphism of \(\mathrm{Over}(\operatorname{Spec}K)\) whose underlying morphism is quasi-compact and whose set-range is a single closed point \(x\) of \(E\). Then \(h^{*}L = 1\) for every Čech Picard class \(L \in \operatorname{Pic}(E)\).

Corollary 35Global sections of the curve

Let \(C\) be a scheme over \(k\) which is proper, geometrically irreducible and geometrically reduced over \(k\). Then the structure morphism induces an isomorphism \(\Gamma (\operatorname{Spec}k, \mathcal{O}_{\operatorname{Spec}k}) \cong \Gamma (C, \mathcal{O}_{C})\); that is, \(\Gamma (C, \mathcal{O}_{C}) = k\).

Corollary 1316Homogeneity of the representing object

Let \(d\) be a Jacobian datum with representing object \(J\), and let \(x, y : \operatorname{Spec}k \to J\) be two \(k\)-points. With the group structure of 1296, the translation \(\tau _{x,y}\) is an automorphism of \(J\) over \(k\) with \(\tau _{x,y} \circ x = y\); on the underlying scheme it commutes with the structure morphism and carries the point of \(x\) to the point of \(y\); and it preserves and reflects membership in the smooth locus of the structure morphism (when the latter is locally of finite presentation), reducedness of stalks, and irreducibility of subsets.

Corollary 181Two-lattice finiteness, localization form

Let \(k\) be a commutative ring and \(N\) a finite module over \(k[T,T^{-1}]\) whose \(k\)-module structure is the restriction of scalars of the \(k[T,T^{-1}]\)-action along the canonical ring map \(k \to k[T,T^{-1}]\). Let \(Q_0, Q_1 \subseteq N\) be \(k\)-submodules such that:

  1. \(Q_0\) is stable under multiplication by \(T\);

  2. \(Q_1\) is stable under multiplication by \(T^{-1}\);

  3. every \(n \in N\) is eventually absorbed by \(Q_0\): there is an integer \(m \ge 0\) with \(T^m \cdot n \in Q_0\);

  4. every \(n \in N\) is eventually absorbed by \(Q_1\): there is an integer \(m \ge 0\) with \(T^{-m} \cdot n \in Q_1\).

Then \(N / (Q_0 + Q_1)\) is a finite \(k\)-module.

LaTeX Lean
Corollary 182Two-lattice finiteness, localization form via powers of the generator

Let \(k\), \(N\), \(Q_0\), \(Q_1\) be as in Corollary 181, satisfying hypotheses (1) and (2) there, and suppose in place of (3) and (4) that:

  1. every \(n \in N\) satisfies: there is an integer \(m \ge 0\) with \(T^m \cdot n \in Q_0\), where \(T^m\) denotes the ordinary \(m\)-th power of the ring element \(T \in k[T,T^{-1}]\);

  2. every \(n \in N\) satisfies: there is an integer \(m \ge 0\) with \(T^{-m} \cdot n \in Q_1\), where \(T^{-m}\) denotes the ordinary \(m\)-th power of \(T^{-1} \in k[T,T^{-1}]\).

Then \(N / (Q_0 + Q_1)\) is a finite \(k\)-module.

Definition 1317Abel source

Let \(d\) be a Jacobian datum with representing object \(J\). An Abel source for \(d\) consists of:

  1. a scheme \(D\) over \(k\);

  2. a certificate that \(D\) is proper over \(k\);

  3. a certificate that \(D\) is geometrically irreducible over \(k\);

  4. an Abel morphism \(a : D \to J\) over \(k\);

  5. a certificate that \(a\) is surjective on underlying topological spaces.

This is a conditional interface: its definition asserts neither the existence of \(D\) nor the existence of \(a\). The intended instance takes \(D\) to be a proper scheme of effective divisors of large degree on \(C\) and \(a\) to be the Abel map.

Definition 1094The Abel Čech class

kleiman-picard, abelian-varieties:page-0107 Let \(P \colon \mathbf{1} \to C\) be a rational point of the curve (a morphism from the unit test). The Abel Čech class on the test \(T = C\) is

\[ \mathcal A_P \; :=\; \mathcal{O}_{C \otimes C}(\Delta ) \cdot \mathcal{O}_{C \otimes C}(P \times C)^{-1} \; \in \; \operatorname{Pic}(C \otimes C), \]

the graph class of the identity \(\operatorname{id}_C\) (the diagonal) times the inverse graph class of the constant point \(C \to \mathbf1 \xrightarrow {P} C\) — both factors through the graph divisor of Definition 151, so one degree certificate serves both. The Abel class \(\alpha _P \in \mathrm{picEt}(C, C)\) is the unit image of its relative class. Milne’s cited section assumes \(g(C){\gt}0\); this graph-class construction uses only the rational point \(P\) and therefore also applies in genus zero.

Definition 1097The Abel element

kleiman-picard, abelian-varieties:page-0107 The Abel element is the Abel class as an element of the degree-zero subgroup,

\[ \alpha _P \in \mathrm{pic}^0(C, C), \]

membership being the certificate of Theorem 1096. On points it is the family \(t \mapsto [\, \Gamma _t - \Gamma _P\, ]\), the divisor-class form \(t \mapsto [t - P]\) of the Abel map with base point \(P\). Definition 941The Amitsur product cover and its insertions

For a pointed cover \(\mathcal W\) of the curve \(X_{B \otimes _A B}\), the Amitsur product cover of \(X_{B \otimes _A (B \otimes _A B)}\) is the common refinement of the three coface pullbacks,

\[ w_{23}^{-1}\mathcal W \ \sqcap \ w_{12}^{-1}\mathcal W \ \sqcap \ w_{13}^{-1}\mathcal W , \]

the curve-product mirror of the Amitsur cover (Definition 826). The three insertions \(v_1, v_2, v_3\) are the pairwise-coincident values of the six coface–coprojection composites \(w_{ij} \circ u_k \colon X_{B \otimes _A (B \otimes _A B)} \to X_B\):

\[ v_1 = w_{12} \circ u_1 = w_{13} \circ u_1, \quad v_2 = w_{23} \circ u_1 = w_{12} \circ u_2, \quad v_3 = w_{23} \circ u_2 = w_{13} \circ u_2 . \]

\[ J_L \; \cong \; d_L.J , \]

Definition 411The second-projection algebra structure on sections

Definition 1175The additive Čech coboundaries

For a two-chart datum as above, the additive coboundary subgroup \(\mathcal B^+(\rho _1, \rho _2) \leq (B, +)\) is \(\rho _1(A_1) + \rho _2(A_2)\); its elements are exactly the sums \(\rho _1(a_1) + \rho _2(a_2)\), equivalently the differences \(\rho _1(a_1) - \rho _2(a_2)\) (replace \(a_2\) by \(-a_2\)). The quotient \(B / \mathcal B^+(\rho _1, \rho _2)\) is the two-cover Čech cokernel — for the section rings of a two-affine cover, the carrier of 345.

Definition 1174The multiplicative Čech coboundaries

For a two-chart datum \(\rho _1 : A_1 \to B\), \(\rho _2 : A_2 \to B\), the coboundary subgroup \(\mathcal B^\times (\rho _1, \rho _2) \leq B^\times \) is the subgroup generated by the images of \(\rho _1^\times \) and \(\rho _2^\times \); its elements are exactly the products \(\rho _1^\times (v_1)\, \rho _2^\times (v_2)\) with \(v_i \in A_i^\times \) (the two images are subgroups, so the products already form a subgroup). The quotient \(B^\times / \mathcal B^\times (\rho _1, \rho _2)\) is the two-cover Čech \(\check H^1\) of units — for a two-affine cover, the Čech Picard group of the cover.

Definition 1177The Čech units reduction

Reduction mod \(\varepsilon \) on units carries thickened coboundaries to coboundaries: by naturality (1169, 1168), \(\mathrm{fst}^\times \bigl(\rho _1[\varepsilon ]^\times (w_1)\, \rho _2[\varepsilon ]^\times (w_2)\bigr) = \rho _1^\times (\mathrm{fst}^\times w_1)\, \rho _2^\times (\mathrm{fst}^\times w_2)\). Hence \(\mathrm{fst}^\times \) descends to a group homomorphism of Čech \(\check H^1\)-of-units groups,

\[ \pi \; :\; B[\varepsilon ]^\times \big/ \mathcal B^\times (\rho _1[\varepsilon ], \rho _2[\varepsilon ]) \longrightarrow B^\times \big/ \mathcal B^\times (\rho _1, \rho _2), \]

the Čech-cocycle incarnation of the restriction \(\operatorname{Pic}(X \times _k \operatorname{Spec}k[\varepsilon ]) \to \operatorname{Pic}(X)\) along \(\varepsilon \mapsto 0\).

Definition 779The Čech–Picard descent homomorphism

For an affine scheme \(X\) with global ring \(A = \Gamma (X,\mathcal{O}_{X})\), the homomorphism of groups

\[ \operatorname {toPic} \colon \operatorname{Pic}(X) \to \operatorname {Pic}(A), \qquad [\mathcal U,\gamma ] \mapsto \bigl(\text{class of the module descended from } \gamma |_{\mathcal W}\bigr), \]

where \(\mathcal W\) is any finite basic refinement of \(\mathcal U\) and \(\gamma |_{\mathcal W}\) is the cocycle obtained by restricting \(\gamma \) along \(\mathcal W \le \mathcal U\).

Definition 966The affine-open Čech–Picard class

Let \(Z\) be a scheme and \(O \subseteq Z\) an affine open. Pullback along the open immersion \(O \hookrightarrow Z\) identifies the ambient sections \(\Gamma (Z, O)\) with the global sections \(\Gamma (O, \top )\) of the open subscheme; write \(\iota _O^{\top }\) for this ring isomorphism. The affine-open class of a Čech Picard class \(L\) on \(Z\) is

\[ L\langle O\rangle \; :=\; \bigl(\iota _O^{\top }\bigr)^{-1}_{*}\, \mathrm{toPic}_O\bigl(\iota ^{*}L\bigr) \; \in \; \operatorname {Pic}\bigl(\Gamma (Z, O)\bigr), \]

the invertible \(\Gamma (Z, O)\)-module obtained by transporting, through the affine Čech–Picard dictionary \(\mathrm{toPic}\) (Definition 779), the restriction of \(L\) to \(O\). It is natural in the open: for affine opens \(O' \le O\) the class \(L\langle O'\rangle \) is the image of \(L\langle O\rangle \) under the restriction homomorphism \(\operatorname {Pic}(\Gamma (Z, O)) \to \operatorname {Pic}(\Gamma (Z, O'))\).

Definition 1107Certified divisor families and the divisor functor value

kleiman-picard A certified divisor family of degree \(n\) over \(R\) is a triple \((d, A, c)\): a local-equation system \(d\) on \(C_R\), a finite chart adaptation \(A\) of \(d\), and a certificate \(c\) of degree \(n\) for \(A\). Divisor equality of the underlying systems (1101) is an equivalence relation on such triples — the adaptation and the certificate are presentation data and do not enter the relation — and

\[ \operatorname{Div}^{\, n}(R) \; :=\; \bigl\{ \, \text{certified divisor families of degree }n\text{ over } R\, \bigr\} \big/ \sim \]

is the value of this certified subfunctor at \(R\). The Picard class descends to it: \(\mathcal{O}(D) \in \operatorname{Pic}(C_R)\) is well defined on \(\operatorname{Div}^{\, n}(R)\). On a certified triple this is the Abel-class map; it agrees with Kleiman’s Abel construction only after the triple is shown to represent a flat effective divisor of degree \(n\). No theorem here says that every effective flat Cartier divisor admits this pinned certificate.

Definition 600The degree homomorphism on the Picard group

The degree descends to a group homomorphism

\[ \deg _{\operatorname{Pic}} : \operatorname{Pic}(X) \to \mathbb {Z}, \qquad \deg _{\operatorname{Pic}}\mathcal{O}_{X}(D) = \deg _K D \quad (D \in \operatorname{Div}(X)), \]

the degree of a Picard class: the degree of any Weil divisor realizing the class. The displayed normalization \(\deg _{\operatorname{Pic}}\mathcal{O}_{X}(D) = \deg _K D\) holds for every Weil divisor \(D\), and is the defining property.

Definition 827An Amitsur-coherent Čech witness

kleiman-picard Let \(\gamma \) be a unit Čech cocycle on a pointed cover \(\mathcal N\) of \(\operatorname{Spec}B\). An Amitsur-coherent Čech witness for \(\gamma \) consists of a pointed cover \(\mathcal V\) of \(\operatorname{Spec}(B \otimes _A B)\) refining both coprojection pullbacks \(q_1^{*}\mathcal N\) and \(q_2^{*}\mathcal N\), together with a unit \(0\)-cochain \(\theta \) on \(\mathcal V\) such that:

  1. (witness) \(\theta \) cobounds the comparison of the two coprojection pullbacks of \(\gamma \): on the overlaps of \(\mathcal V\), \(\theta _x \cdot (q_1^{\sharp }\gamma )_{xy} = (q_2^{\sharp }\gamma )_{xy} \cdot \theta _y\);

  2. (coherent) on the Amitsur refinement \(\mathcal V_{123}\), the three coface pullbacks of \(\theta \) satisfy the Amitsur cocycle relation \((f_{23}^{\sharp }\theta ) \cdot (f_{12}^{\sharp }\theta ) = f_{13}^{\sharp }\theta \).

The witness relation records, at cocycle level, the class equality \(q_1^{*} N = q_2^{*} N\) for \(N = [\mathcal N, \gamma ]\); the coherence relation is the triple-overlap cocycle identity that lets \(\theta \) itself descend.

Definition 832The comparison cover on the curve product

On the curve product \(X_{B \otimes B} := C \otimes \operatorname{Spec}(B \otimes _A B)\), the comparison cover of a witness cover \(\mathcal V\) of \(\operatorname{Spec}(B \otimes _A B)\) and an upstairs cover \(\mathcal A\) of \(X_B := C \otimes \operatorname{Spec}B\) is the pointwise intersection

\[ \mathrm{pr}^{*}\mathcal V \; \sqcap \; \bigl(u_1^{*}\mathcal A \sqcap u_2^{*}\mathcal A\bigr), \]

where \(\mathrm{pr} \colon X_{B \otimes B} \to \operatorname{Spec}(B \otimes _A B)\) is the projection and \(u_1, u_2 = C \lhd q_1, C \lhd q_2 \colon X_{B \otimes B} \to X_B\) are the whiskered coprojections.

Definition 402The same-carrier comparison at an affine test

Let \(k \to L\) be a field extension, \(\sigma : \operatorname{Spec}L \to \operatorname{Spec}k\) the induced morphism, \(C \in \mathrm{Over}(\operatorname{Spec}k)\) with base change \(\sigma ^{*}C \in \mathrm{Over}(\operatorname{Spec}L)\) (12), and \(A\) an algebra in a scalar tower \(k \to L \to A\). \[ \bigl(\sigma ^{*}C \otimes (\operatorname{Spec}A/\operatorname{Spec}L)\bigr)_{\mathrm{left}} \; \cong \; \bigl(C \otimes (\operatorname{Spec}A/\operatorname{Spec}k)\bigr)_{\mathrm{left}} \]

Definition 398The cross-base comparison isomorphism

In the situation of 397, the cross-base comparison isomorphism is the isomorphism of schemes

\[ (f^{*}X \otimes T)_{\mathrm{left}} \; \cong \; (X \otimes f_{!}T)_{\mathrm{left}} \]

identifying the two pullbacks of the common cospan \(X_{\mathrm{left}} \to S \leftarrow T_{\mathrm{left}}\): the left-hand side by the cross-base pasted square (397), the right-hand side by the product bridge for \(X\) and \(f_{!}T\) over \(S\) (394). Definition 490Termwise base change of the two-cover complex of the curve

Definition 507Weil divisors on a curve

papaioannou-algebraic-rr:page-0006 For an integral scheme \(X\) with generic point \(\eta \), a Weil divisor is a finitely supported \(\mathbb {Z}\)-valued function on the non-generic points, i.e. an element of the free abelian group

\[ \operatorname{Div}(X) \; =\; \bigl(\{ x \in X : x \neq \eta \} \to _{\mathrm{fin}} \mathbb {Z}\bigr) \]

on the set of non-generic points. It carries the pointwise abelian-group structure and the pointwise partial order, both independent of any base field. For the curve \(X\) the non-generic points are exactly the closed points (503), so a Weil divisor is a finite formal \(\mathbb {Z}\)-combination of closed points.

Definition 258Depth of a module

stacks-project Let \(R\) be a commutative ring, \(I \subseteq R\) an ideal and \(M\) an \(R\)-module. An \(M\)-regular sequence is a finite sequence \(x_1, \dots , x_n \in R\) such that each \(x_i\) is a non-zero-divisor on \(M/(x_1, \dots , x_{i-1})M\) and \((x_1, \dots , x_n)M \neq M\). The \(I\)-depth of \(M\) is the element \(\mathrm{depth}_I(M)\) of \(\{ 0, 1, 2, \dots , \infty \} \) defined by:

  1. if \(IM = M\), then \(\mathrm{depth}_I(M) = \infty \);

  2. otherwise, \(\mathrm{depth}_I(M)\) is the supremum of the lengths of \(M\)-regular sequences contained in \(I\) (the supremum of the empty set being \(0\)).

When \((R, \mathfrak m)\) is local, \(\mathrm{depth}(M) := \mathrm{depth}_{\mathfrak m}(M)\) is called simply the depth of \(M\).

Definition 138The diagonal of the curve square

kleiman-picard The diagonal of \(C \otimes C\) is the morphism into the product determined by the identity in both components,

\[ \delta \; :=\; \langle \operatorname{id}_C, \operatorname{id}_C \rangle \colon C \longrightarrow C \otimes C, \qquad \mathrm{fst} \circ \delta = \operatorname{id}_C, \quad \mathrm{snd} \circ \delta = \operatorname{id}_C . \]

For opens \(U, V\) of \(C\) its preimage of a product chart is the intersection of the factors, \(\delta ^{-1}\mathfrak W(U,V) = U \cap V\). If moreover \(C\) is separated over \(\operatorname{Spec}k\), then \(\delta \) is a closed immersion; its image \(\Delta := \delta (C)\) is closed, with open complement \(\Delta ^{\mathrm{c}} := (C \otimes C) \setminus \Delta \); and the support of the kernel ideal sheaf of \(\delta \) is exactly \(\Delta \).

Definition 139The diagonal member and its equation

Let \(\vartheta \in \Gamma (C \otimes C, \mathfrak W(U,U))\) be the section identified with \(1 - \mathrm{elift}\) (Definition 134). The diagonal member attached to the chart \(U\) is the affine basic open

\[ \mathfrak D(U) \; :=\; D(\vartheta ) \; \subseteq \; \mathfrak W(U,U). \]

The diagonal equation \(e_U \in \Gamma (C \otimes C, \mathfrak D(U))\) is the restriction to \(\mathfrak D(U)\) of the section of \(\mathfrak W(U,U)\) identified with the diagonal generator \(u \otimes 1 - 1 \otimes u\). Writing \(\xi _x\) for the section of \(\mathfrak W(U,U)\) identified with \(x \in B \otimes _k B\), the pullback along the diagonal is multiplication: over \(\delta ^{-1}\mathfrak W(U,U) = U\),

\[ \delta ^\sharp (\xi _x) \; =\; \mu (x) \; \in \; \Gamma (C, U), \qquad \mu \colon B \otimes _k B \to B, \quad x \otimes y \mapsto xy . \]

Consequently, if \(\mu (\mathrm{elift}) = 0\), then \(\delta ^{-1}\mathfrak D(U) = U\).

Definition 144The frozen chart data of a smooth curve

Let \(C\) be smooth of relative dimension one over \(\operatorname{Spec}k\). Then every point \(p\) of \(C\) has an affine open \(U \ni p\) whose section ring \(B := \Gamma (C, U)\) carries an étale \(k[X]\)-algebra structure — an étale coordinate \(u \in B\) — compatible with the section \(k\)-algebra structure (making \(k \to k[X] \to B\) a tower).

A chart datum for \(C\) is a choice, one per point \(p\), of such a chart \(\mathrm{chart}(p) \ni p\) with its étale coordinate. On each chart the coordinate is flat, formally unramified and essentially of finite type, so the packaged diagonal localisation (Theorem 228) supplies a frozen idempotent lift \(\mathrm{elift}(p) \in B \otimes _k B\) with \(\mu _k(\mathrm{elift}(p)) = 0\), whose base change is idempotent and generates the \(k[X]\)-diagonal ideal.

Definition 222The diagonal equation and the base-change collapse

The diagonal equation is

\[ \delta \; :=\; u \otimes 1 - 1 \otimes u \; \in \; B \otimes _k B . \]

The base-change collapse is the \(k\)-algebra homomorphism

\[ \pi \colon B \otimes _k B \longrightarrow B \otimes _{k[X]} B, \qquad x \otimes y \mapsto x \otimes y, \]

the surjection identifying the two tensor squares. It satisfies:

  • \(\mu _k(\delta ) = 0\): the diagonal equation lies in the \(k\)-diagonal ideal;

  • \(\pi (\delta ) = 0\): the collapse kills the diagonal equation, because \(u \otimes 1 = 1 \otimes u\) already in \(B \otimes _{k[X]} B\) (here \(u = X \cdot 1\) is a scalar of the tensor product);

  • \(\mu _{k[X]} \circ \pi = \mu _k\): the two multiplications agree through the collapse.

abelian-varieties:page-0023 Let \(X\) be a scheme smooth over \(k\) whose self-product \(X \times _k X\) is integral, and let \(G\) be a group scheme locally of finite type over \(k\). For a rational map \(f : X \dashrightarrow G\) over \(k\), the difference rational map

\[ \Phi \; :\; X \times _k X \dashrightarrow G, \qquad \Phi (x, y) = f(x)\, f(y)^{-1}, \]

is the composite \(\delta _G \circ \bigl(f \circ \mathrm{pr}_1,\ f \circ \mathrm{pr}_2\bigr)\): precompose \(f\) with the two (open, by 1226) projections, pair the results into \(G \times _k G\) (1212; both factors are over \(k\) by 1203, and the pairing needs the integrality of \(X \times _k X\)), and post-compose with the difference morphism \(\delta _G\).

Definition 1111The auxiliary locally certified divisor functor \(\operatorname{Div}^{\, n}_{\mathrm{Zar}}\)

The value at \(R\) of the locally certified divisor functor is

\[ \operatorname{Div}^{\, n}_{\mathrm{Zar}}(R) \; :=\; \bigl\{ \, d \text{ locally certified of degree } n \text{ on } C_R \, \bigr\} \big/ \sim , \]

the quotient by divisor equality (well posed by 1109). The Picard class descends to it, and passing from a global to a local certificate gives a natural comparison \(\operatorname{Div}^{\, n}(R) \to \operatorname{Div}^{\, n}_{\mathrm{Zar}}(R)\) compatible with the Picard class.

This is the auxiliary carrier used by the statements in this section. The widened representability route uses the separate arbitrary-affine carrier described above. The reason for retaining this auxiliary carrier is Theorem 1108: the condition “carries a global certificate” is not local on \(\operatorname{Spec}R\), so \(\operatorname{Div}^{\, n}\) cannot be a Zariski sheaf on affine test algebras, whereas \(\operatorname{Div}^{\, n}_{\mathrm{Zar}}\) is local on the base by construction.

Definition 1103Finite chart adaptation of a local-equation system

kleiman-picard Let \(d\) be a local-equation system on \(C_R\), adapted to a pointed cover \(\mathcal U\). \[ f_j\big|_{P_j \cap \mathcal U(y)} \; =\; u \cdot d_y\big|_{P_j \cap \mathcal U(y)} . \]

(The quantifier ranges over all \(y\); over an empty overlap the section ring is the zero ring and the clause is vacuous.)

In particular, anchored data suffice to build an adaptation: if for each \(j\) one is given a point \(p_j\) with \(P_j \subseteq \mathcal U(p_j)\) and a unit \(w_j\) on \(P_j\) with \(f_j = w_j \cdot d_{p_j}|_{P_j}\), then the refinement clause holds for every \(y\), with unit the product of \(w_j|\) and the restriction of the transition unit \(g_{p_j y}\) of \(d\) (984).

Definition 993The class of a Weil divisor

For a Weil divisor \(D \in \operatorname{Div}(X)\) (507), its Picard class is the finite product

\[ \mathcal{O}_{X}(D) = \prod _{x} \mathcal{O}_{X}(x)^{D_x} \in \operatorname{Pic}(X), \]

Definition 525Sections of the divisor sheaf

papaioannou-algebraic-rr:page-0007 For a Weil divisor \(D\) and a nonempty open \(U\), the sections of \(\mathcal O(D)\) over \(U\) are

\[ \mathcal O(D)(U) = \{ g \in K(X) : \text{at every closed point } x \in U,\ g \text{ has pole order} \le D_x \} , \]

the rational functions with poles bounded by \(D\) on \(U\); over the empty open the sections are the zero module (forced by the sheaf condition, since the empty sieve covers \(\bot \)). This is a \(K\)-submodule of \(K(X)\): it contains \(0\); it is closed under addition because a valuation is subadditive, \(\mathrm{ord}_x(g_1 + g_2) \ge \min (\mathrm{ord}_x g_1, \mathrm{ord}_x g_2)\), so the pole bound is preserved; and closed under \(K\)-scaling because constants have no poles (524).

Definition 1114The window submodule and the embedding \(\varepsilon \)

nitsure-hilbert-quot Let \(a\) be an exponent at which the relative twist \(\mathcal{O}(aF)\) on \(C_R\) has vanishing \(H^1\), so that base change identifies

\[ R \otimes _k H_a \; \xrightarrow {\ \sim \ }\; H^0\bigl(C_R, \mathcal{O}(aF)\bigr). \]

For a local-equation system \(d\) on \(C_R\), the window submodule

\[ K_a(d) \; \subseteq \; R \otimes _k H_a \]

is the preimage under this identification of the submodule of sections of \(\mathcal{O}(aF)\) vanishing along \(d\) — i.e. of \(H^0(C_R, \mathcal{O}(aF - D))\), read inside the free window. It depends only on \(d\), not on any chart adaptation, and it is unchanged when \(d\) is replaced by a divisor-equal system; hence it descends to \(\operatorname{Div}^{\, n}(R)\) and to \(\operatorname{Div}^{\, n}_{\mathrm{Zar}}(R)\).

Taking the two pinned exponents gives the window pair

\[ \varepsilon (D) \; =\; \bigl(K_M(D),\, K_{M+s}(D)\bigr) \; \in \; \Bigl(R \otimes _k H_M \ \text{submodules}\Bigr) \times \Bigl(R \otimes _k H_{M+s}\ \text{submodules}\Bigr). \]

Definition 1122The affine pullback package

An affine pullback package for \(\mathbf{Div}\) consists of, for every \(k\)-algebra \(S\), a map

\[ \rho _S \colon \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Over}(\operatorname{Spec}k)}\bigl(\operatorname{Spec}S, \mathbf{Div}_{/k}\bigr) \longrightarrow \operatorname{Div}^{\, g}_{\mathrm{Zar}}(S), \]

subject to two conditions: \(\rho _S(v)\) is classified by \(v\) in the sense of 1119, for every \(v\); and \(\rho \) is natural, \(\rho _B(\varphi \circ v) = \varphi _* \rho _A(v)\) for every \(k\)-algebra map \(\varphi \colon A \to B\).

The canonical way to produce such a \(\rho \) is from a chart family: a certified divisor family \(U_{ij}\) over the coordinate ring of each affine chart of \(\mathbf{Div}\), pulled back along a chart presentation of the given \(v\); this is well defined precisely when the family is compatible, meaning that two chart presentations inducing the same morphism to \(\mathbf{Div}\) pull \(U\) back to the same class in \(\operatorname{Div}^{\, g}_{\mathrm{Zar}}\).

Definition 1118The divisor scheme \(\mathbf{Div}\)

nitsure-hilbert-quot, kleiman-picard Choose \(k\)-bases of \(H_M\) and \(H_{M+s}\), giving the Grassmannian functors \(\mathrm{Gr}(H_M, g)\) and \(\mathrm{Gr}(H_{M+s}, g)\) their standard affine charts indexed by coordinate subsets, and let \(\mathrm{Gr}\text{-pair}\) be the product of the two chart-glued Grassmannian schemes. For \(\sigma \in H_s = H^0(C, \mathcal{O}(sF))\), multiplication by \(\sigma \) is a \(k\)-linear map \(\mu _\sigma \colon H_M \to H_{M+s}\).

The divisor scheme \(\mathbf{Div}\) is the closed subscheme of \(\mathrm{Gr}\text{-pair}\) cut out, chart by chart, by the ideal generated by the matrix entries of the composites

\[ K_1 \; \hookrightarrow \; R \otimes _k H_M \; \xrightarrow {\ \operatorname{id}\otimes \mu _\sigma \ }\; R \otimes _k H_{M+s} \; \twoheadrightarrow \; (R \otimes _k H_{M+s})/K_2 , \qquad \sigma \in H_s , \]

where \((K_1, K_2)\) is the tautological pair on the chart. Its \(R\)-points are therefore the pairs \((K_1, K_2)\) of Grassmannian points of corank \(g\) satisfying \(\mu _\sigma (K_1) \subseteq K_2\) for every \(\sigma \in H_s\). It comes with a closed immersion \(\mathbf{Div} \hookrightarrow \mathrm{Gr}\text{-pair}\); in particular morphisms into \(\mathbf{Div}\) are determined by their composites with that immersion. Placed over \(\operatorname{Spec}k\) by its structure morphism, it is an object \(\mathbf{Div}_{/k}\) of \(\mathrm{Over}(\operatorname{Spec}k)\).

Definition 689Presented étale cover

A presented étale cover \(E\) of \(A\) consists of a natural number \(n\), an ideal \(I\) of the polynomial ring \(A[x_1,\dots ,x_n]\), a proof that the quotient algebra \(B_E := A[x_1,\dots ,x_n]/I\) is étale over \(A\), and a proof that the induced map of spectra \(\operatorname{Spec}B_E \to \operatorname{Spec}A\) is surjective. We call \(B_E\) the carrier of \(E\). Since étale algebras are flat, surjectivity of \(\operatorname{Spec}B_E \to \operatorname{Spec}A\) together with flatness makes \(B_E\) faithfully flat over \(A\).

Definition 647The denominator lattice and its exhaustion

The denominator lattice \(A_n\) of \(\mathcal{O}_{Y}(D + nF)\) is the join, inside \(K(Y)\), of the section lattices over the two charts:

\[ A_n \; =\; \mathcal{O}_{Y}(D + nF)(V_0) \; +\; \mathcal{O}_{Y}(D + nF)(V_1) \qquad (\text{as } K\text{-submodules of } K(Y)). \]

It lies in the fixed ambient \(N := \mathcal{O}_{Y}(D)(V_0 \cap V_1)\), the lattices form an increasing chain, and they exhaust \(N\):

Definition 644The fibre Weil divisor

The fibre Weil divisor \(F\) is the effective part of \(\mathrm{div}(u)\): the Weil divisor (507) with coefficient \(F_x = \max (\mathrm{ord}_x(u), 0)\) at each closed point \(x\). It is effective (\(F \ge 0\)); it vanishes on \(V_1\) (\(F_x = 0\) for \(x \in V_1\)); it agrees with \(\mathrm{div}(u)\) on \(V_0\) (\(F_x = \mathrm{ord}_x(u)\) for \(x \in V_0\)); and its degree is nonnegative. If moreover some closed point \(x_0 \in V_0\) lies outside \(V_1\) — a point of the fibre over \([1 : 0]\) — then \(F\) is nonzero and has strictly positive degree.

Definition 1105The chart colength modules and their glued equalizer

Let \(A\) be a finite chart adaptation of \(d\), with pieces \(P_j\) and equations \(f_j\). Its chart colength modules are the \(R\)-algebras

\[ Q_j \; :=\; \mathcal{O}_{}(P_j) \big/ (f_j), \]

the structure sheaves of the pieces of the divisor cut out by \(d\). On an overlap put \(Q_{ij} := \mathcal{O}_{}(P_i \cap P_j)/(f_i|, f_j|)\), the quotient by the ideal generated by both restricted equations, and let \(\delta ^-, \delta ^+ \colon \prod _j Q_j \to \prod _{(i,j)} Q_{ij}\) be the two restriction maps, \(\delta ^-\) restricting the \(i\)-component and \(\delta ^+\) the \(j\)-component. \[ W(A) \; :=\; \ker \bigl(\delta ^- - \delta ^+\bigr) \; \subseteq \; \prod _j Q_j , \]

an \(R\)-submodule; concretely \(s \in W(A)\) iff \(s_i\) and \(s_j\) have the same image in \(Q_{ij}\) for every pair \((i,j)\). It is the module of global sections of the structure sheaf of the divisor over the union of the pieces.

Definition 1113The affine Grassmannian functor

the \(R\)-dimensions of the degree-zero and degree-one cohomology, and

Definition 1106The colength certificate of degree \(n\)

kleiman-picard A finite chart adaptation \(A\) is certified of degree \(n\) if

  1. every chart colength module \(Q_j\) is finite and projective over \(R\);

  2. the glued colength module \(W(A)\) is finite and projective over \(R\), and has constant rank \(n\) at every prime: \(\operatorname {rank}_{\mathfrak p} W(A) = n\) for all \(\mathfrak p \in \operatorname{Spec}R\);

  3. the cokernel of the inclusion \(W(A) \hookrightarrow \prod _j Q_j\) is flat over \(R\);

  4. the cokernel of \(\delta ^- - \delta ^+\) is flat over \(R\).

Clauses (c1) and (c2) say that the divisor is finite flat of degree \(n\) over the base — Kleiman’s condition that a relative effective divisor of degree \(n\) have \(S\)-flat structure sheaf with fibres of length \(n\). Clauses (c3) and (c4) are what make the certificate stable under an arbitrary base change \(R \to R'\): they are the flatness hypotheses under which tensoring the defining left-exact sequence \(0 \to W(A) \to \prod _j Q_j \to \prod _{ij} Q_{ij}\) with \(R'\) stays exact, so that the base-changed glued module is again the equalizer of the base-changed arrows. Over a field they are automatic.

Definition 1119The characterizing clause of a classifying morphism

Let \(S\) be a \(k\)-algebra, \(D \in \operatorname{Div}^{\, g}_{\mathrm{Zar}}(S)\), and \(v \colon \operatorname{Spec}S \to \mathbf{Div}\) a morphism. Say \(v\) classifies \(D\) if for every \(k\)-algebra \(T\) under \(S\), every certified family \(G\) over \(T\) whose class is the restriction of \(D\) to \(T\), and every presentation of \(\varepsilon (G)\) as a point of a chart of \(\mathrm{Gr}\text{-pair}\) — that is, a \(k\)-algebra map \(w\) from the chart ring to \(T\) carrying the tautological pair to \(\varepsilon (G)\) — the square

\[ \operatorname{Spec}T \longrightarrow \operatorname{Spec}S \xrightarrow {\ v\ } \mathbf{Div} \hookrightarrow \mathrm{Gr}\text{-pair} \]

agrees with the chart morphism \(\operatorname{Spec}T \xrightarrow {w} \mathrm{Gr}\text{-pair}\).

Quantifying over all tests \(T\), all certified representatives and all chart presentations makes the clause stable under refinement of covers and change of representative by construction.

Definition 1109The Zariski-local certificate

A local-equation system \(d\) on \(C_R\) is locally certified of degree \(n\) if there are finitely many \(g_1, \dots , g_m \in R\) generating the unit ideal such that for each \(i\) there is a certified divisor family of degree \(n\) over the localisation \(R_{g_i}\) whose local-equation system is divisor-equal to the pullback of \(d\) along \(C_{R_{g_i}} \to C_R\).

Being locally certified is invariant under divisor equality, and every certified family is locally certified.

Definition 1295Jacobian datum

A Jacobian datum for \(C\) consists of:

  1. a scheme \(J\) over \(k\);

  2. a representation of the degree-zero relative Picard functor by \(J\): a family of bijections \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Over}(\operatorname{Spec}k)}(T, J) \cong \mathrm{pic}^0(C, T)\), natural in the test object \(T\);

  3. the certificate that the structure morphism of \(J\) is locally of finite type;

  4. the certificate that the structure morphism of \(J\) is quasi-compact.

The two certificates come from the construction of the representing object and are carried as part of the datum rather than re-derived.

A system of local equations on \(X\), adapted to a pointed cover \(\mathcal U\), consists of a section \(f_x \in \mathcal{O}_{X}(\mathcal U(x))\) on each member, subject to two conditions:

  • (regularity) the germ of \(f_x\) at every point \(y \in \mathcal U(x)\) is a nonzerodivisor in the stalk \(\mathcal{O}_{X,y}\);

  • (overlap) for every pair \(x, y\) the restrictions of \(f_x\) and \(f_y\) to the overlap \(\mathcal U(x) \cap \mathcal U(y)\) differ by a unit factor: there is a unit \(u \in \mathcal{O}_{X}(\mathcal U(x) \cap \mathcal U(y))^{\times }\) with \(f_x|_{\cap } = u \cdot f_y|_{\cap }\).

Definition 986The Picard class of a local-equation system

The transition units \(g_{xy}\) of a local-equation system \(d\) form a unit Čech \(1\)-cocycle on its cover \(\mathcal U\); its class

\[ \mathrm{picClass}(d) = [\mathcal U,\, g] \in \operatorname{Pic}(X) \]

is the Picard class \(\mathcal{O}_{X}(D)\) of the effective divisor \(D\) cut out by \(d\).

Definition 988Pullback of a local-equation system

Let \(f \colon Y \to X\) be a morphism of schemes and \(E\) a local-equation system on \(X\) (983), adapted to a pointed cover \(\mathcal U\). Pull the cover back pointwise: the pulled-back pointed cover \(f^{*}\mathcal U\) assigns to \(y \in Y\) the open \(f^{-1}\mathcal U(f(y))\). The pulled-back equations are the \(f\)-pullbacks \(f^{*}\bigl(f_{f(y)}\bigr) \in \mathcal{O}_{Y}\bigl(f^{-1}\mathcal U(f(y))\bigr)\) of the equations of \(E\).

These form a local-equation system \(f^{*}E\) on \(f^{*}\mathcal U\), under the additional hypothesis that the pulled-back equations are regular: that the germ of \(f^{*}(f_{f(y)})\) at every point of its member is a nonzerodivisor. This regularity is not automatic — pulling a nonzerodivisor back along a non-flat morphism can produce a zerodivisor, so the naive claim “pull the equations back and stay a local-equation system” is false in general, and the hypothesis is genuinely required. (Flatness of \(f\) would be a stronger sufficient condition, since flat pullback preserves nonzerodivisors; it is not assumed here.)

Definition 401Pushing an affine test down a field extension

Let \(k \to L\) be a field extension, \(\sigma : \operatorname{Spec}L \to \operatorname{Spec}k\) the induced morphism, and \(A\) an \(L\)-algebra whose \(k\)-algebra structure is the restriction through \(L\) (a scalar tower \(k \to L \to A\)). Write \(\operatorname{Spec}A / \operatorname{Spec}F\) for the affine test attached to an \(F\)-algebra \(A\): the object \(\operatorname{Spec}A\) of \(\mathrm{Over}(\operatorname{Spec}F)\) with structure morphism \(\operatorname{Spec}\) of the algebra map. Then pushing the affine test of \(A\) over \(L\) forward along \(\sigma \) gives the affine test of \(A\) over \(k\): there is an isomorphism

\[ \sigma _{!}\bigl(\operatorname{Spec}A / \operatorname{Spec}L\bigr) \; \cong \; \operatorname{Spec}A / \operatorname{Spec}k \quad \text{in } \mathrm{Over}(\operatorname{Spec}k), \]

Definition 327Mayer–Vietoris square

Provided by Mathlib. Let \((\mathcal C, J)\) be a small site. A Mayer–Vietoris square consists of four objects \(X_1, X_2, X_3, X_4\) of \(\mathcal C\) and morphisms \(f_{12} : X_1 \to X_2\), \(f_{13} : X_1 \to X_3\), \(f_{24} : X_2 \to X_4\), \(f_{34} : X_3 \to X_4\) such that the two composites \(X_1 \to X_2 \to X_4\) and \(X_1 \to X_3 \to X_4\) agree, \(f_{13}\) is a monomorphism, and, after applying the representable-presheaf-then-sheafification functor \(\mathcal C \to \mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C, J; \mathrm{Set})\), the resulting square of sheaves of sets is a pushout square: the image of \(X_4\) is the pushout, over the image of \(X_1\), of the images of \(X_2\) and \(X_3\). The prototypical example is \(X_1 = U \cap V\), \(X_2 = U\), \(X_3 = V\), \(X_4 = U \cup V\) for two opens \(U, V\) of a topological space, with the evident inclusions.

Definition 998Meromorphic presentation

A meromorphic presentation of a Čech Picard class on an integral scheme \(X\) consists of a pointed cover \(\mathcal U\), a unit Čech \(1\)-cocycle \(\gamma \) on \(\mathcal U\), and a family \((f_x)_x\) of units \(f_x \in K(X)^{\times }\), one per member, satisfying the ratio law

\[ f_x \cdot f_y^{-1} = \mathrm{germ}_\eta (\gamma _{xy}) \qquad \text{for every pair } x, y, \]

where \(\gamma _{xy} \in \Gamma (X, \mathcal U(x) \cap \mathcal U(y))^{\times }\) is the cocycle value. Its Picard class is

\[ \mathrm{picClass}(P) = [\mathcal U, \gamma ] \in \operatorname{Pic}(X). \]

Definition 1260The Milne 3.3 indeterminacy property

abelian-varieties:page-0023 A rational map \(f : X \dashrightarrow G\) has the Milne 3.3 indeterminacy property if its indeterminacy locus is empty or of pure codimension one, in the following precise sense: either \(Z(f) = \emptyset \), or every \(x \in Z(f)\) satisfies

\[ \exists \, z \in Z(f), \quad \operatorname {coheight}(z) = 1 \ \text{ and }\ x \in \overline{\{ z\} } . \]

(The requirement \(z \in Z(f)\) is essential: on a variety every non-generic point is a specialisation of some codimension-one point, so without it the second alternative would be nearly vacuous, and in particular too weak to combine with the codimension-\(\geq 2\) bound of 1261.)

Milne’s Lemma 3.3 asserts that every rational map over an algebraically closed field \(\bar k\) from a nonsingular \(\bar k\)-variety to a group \(\bar k\)-variety has this property; this is 1291, proved in §11.8 from the substeps developed here (1231, 1232, 1233, 1240, 1238, 1243) together with the row argument, the germ-range spreading criterion and the codimension-one transport of §11.7. The consumers in §11.9 nevertheless take the property as an explicit hypothesis.

Definition 1086The canonical slice morphism of an equality

Let \(\mathcal C\) be a category, \(S\) an object, and \(a = b\) two equal morphisms \(T \to S\). The identity of \(T\) is a morphism of slice objects \((T, a) \to (T, b)\) in \(\mathrm{Over}(S)\), the canonical morphism of the equality. It satisfies: the canonical morphism of a reflexive equality is the identity; canonical morphisms compose to the canonical morphism of the transitive equality; and every slice morphism \(g \colon X \to (T, b)\) factors as the canonical morphism of its own compatibility equation followed by the slice morphism induced by its underlying map.

Definition 784The descended module of a cocycle

Let \(u\) be a descent \(1\)-cocycle relative to \(A \to B\). The descended \(A\)-module of \(u\) is the \(A\)-submodule

\[ \mathrm{descended}(u) := \{ \, x \in B : u \cdot (x \otimes 1) = 1 \otimes x \, \} \subseteq B, \]

the equalizer of the two \(A\)-linear maps \(B \to B \otimes _A B\), \(x \mapsto u \cdot (x \otimes 1)\) and \(x \mapsto 1 \otimes x\); equivalently, the descended module of the descent datum on the \(B\)-module \(B\) whose coaction is \(x \mapsto u \cdot (x \otimes 1)\) (counitality is the normalization condition and coassociativity is the cocycle identity).

Definition 783Descent \(1\)-cocycle

A descent \(1\)-cocycle relative to \(A \to B\) is a unit \(u \in (B \otimes _A B)^{\times }\) such that:

  1. (normalization) \(\mu (u) = 1\);

  2. (cocycle identity) \(\partial _{23}(u) \cdot \partial _{12}(u) = \partial _{13}(u)\) in \(B \otimes _A (B \otimes _A B)\).

When \(B = \prod _i A_{f_i}\) is a finite product of localizations covering \(\operatorname{Spec}A\), this is exactly a Čech \(1\)-cocycle of units on the cover by the basic opens \(D(f_i)\).

Definition 786Base change of the tensor square and tensor cube of a cover

\[ B \otimes _A B \; \longrightarrow \; (A' \otimes _A B) \otimes _{A'} (A' \otimes _A B), \qquad x \otimes y \mapsto (1 \otimes x) \otimes (1 \otimes y). \]

Likewise, the base change of the tensor cube is the canonical \(A\)-algebra homomorphism on triple tensor products

\[ B \otimes _A (B \otimes _A B) \; \longrightarrow \; (A' \otimes _A B) \otimes _{A'} \bigl( (A' \otimes _A B) \otimes _{A'} (A' \otimes _A B) \bigr), \qquad x \otimes (y \otimes z) \mapsto (1 \otimes x) \otimes \bigl( (1 \otimes y) \otimes (1 \otimes z) \bigr). \]

Definition 938The \(\sigma \)-normalized comparison datum

Fix a unit Čech cocycle \(\gamma \) on a pointed cover \(\mathcal N\) of \(X_B\), representing a class \(L = [\gamma ]\). A \(\sigma \)-normalized comparison of \(\gamma \) packages:

  • a trivializing \(0\)-cochain \(\rho \) of the section-pullback \(s_B^{\sharp }\gamma \) on the cover \(s_B^{-1}\mathcal N\) of \(\operatorname{Spec}B\): \(\rho _b \cdot (s_B^{\sharp }\gamma )_{b b'} = \rho _{b'}\) on overlaps — the cochain shadow of rigidification (926) along the section over \(B\);

  • a pointed cover \(\mathcal W\) of \(X_{B \otimes _A B}\) refining both coprojection pullbacks of \(\mathcal N\), and a comparison \(0\)-cochain \(\theta \) on it, with

  • (N1) \(\theta _x \cdot (u_1^{\sharp }\gamma )_{x y} = (u_2^{\sharp }\gamma )_{x y} \cdot \theta _y\) on overlaps — \(\theta \) cobounds the two coprojection pullbacks of \(\gamma \), realising \(u_1^{*} L = u_2^{*} L\) at the cochain level; and

  • (N2) \((s_q^{\sharp }\theta )_y \cdot (q_2^{\sharp }\rho )_y = (q_1^{\sharp }\rho )_y\) on the normalization cover (937) — the \(\sigma \)-restriction of \(\theta \) is the \(\rho \)-comparison \(q_1^{\sharp }\rho / q_2^{\sharp }\rho \).

The normalization is \(\rho \)-relative: rigidification makes \(s_B^{\sharp }\gamma \) trivial only as a class, giving the trivializing cochain \(\rho \), so “\(\sigma \)-restriction \(=1\)” is replaced by (N2). Every step is stated pointwise via unit pullback and is blind to disconnectedness of \(\operatorname{Spec}(B \otimes _A B)\).

Definition 916The pullback-value property

Let \(f \colon T' \to T\) be a morphism of test objects, \(s \in \mathrm{picEt}(C, T)\), and \(W\) an affine open of \(T'_{\mathrm{left}}\). A plus class \(v \in \mathrm{PicEtAff}(C, \Gamma (T', W))\) has the pullback-value property for \((f, s, W)\) if, for every affine open \(W_0 \subseteq W\) contained in the preimage \(f^{-1}V\) of some affine open \(V\) of \(T_{\mathrm{left}}\), the restriction of \(v\) to \(\Gamma (T', W_0)\) equals the pullback of \(s_V\) along the section-pullback homomorphism \(\Gamma (T, V) \to \Gamma (T', W_0)\) (pullback of sections along \(f\), a \(k\)-algebra map; Definition 744).

Definition 1076Compatible local data on an open cover

Let \(T\) be a test object and \((O_i)_{i \in \iota }\) an open cover of \(T_{\mathrm{left}}\). Compatible local data on the cover is a family assigning to every index \(i\) and every affine open \(W \le O_i\) a plus class \(v_{i,W} \in \mathrm{PicEtAff}(C, \Gamma (T,W))\), such that (res) within a member, \(v_{i,W}\) restricts to \(v_{i,W'}\) for \(W' \le W \le O_i\), and (glue) across members, \(v_{i,W} = v_{j,W}\) whenever \(W \le O_i\) and \(W \le O_j\). A plus class \(z\) at an affine open \(W\) is a glue value of the data when its restriction to every affine sub-open \(W_0 \le W\) contained in some member \(O_i\) equals \(v_{i,W_0}\).

Definition 1138A rank-one local presentation of a Picard class

Let \(T\) be a \(k\)-scheme, let \(f_T\colon C_T\to T\), and let \(\lambda \in \mathrm{pic}^{g(C)}(C,T)\). \[ R^1f_{i*}\mathcal L_i=0, \qquad \mathcal N_i:=f_{i*}\mathcal L_i\text{ is invertible}, \]

The equation \([\mathcal L_i]=p_i^*\lambda \) is part of the data; a line bundle unrelated to \(\lambda \) is not a presentation of it. Definition 134The sections identification

Let \(U\) and \(V\) be affine. The square of section rings

\[ \begin{array}{ccc} \Gamma (\operatorname{Spec}k, \mathcal{O}_{}) & \longrightarrow & \Gamma (X, U) \\ \downarrow & & \downarrow \\ \Gamma (T, V) & \longrightarrow & \Gamma \bigl(X \otimes T,\ \mathfrak W(U,V)\bigr) \end{array} \]

— the top and left edges the pullbacks along the two structure morphisms to \(\operatorname{Spec}k\), the bottom and right edges the two projection pullbacks \(\mathrm{fst}^\sharp \), \(\mathrm{snd}^\sharp \) — is a pushout of commutative rings. Since \(\Gamma (\operatorname{Spec}k, \mathcal{O}_{}) = k\), it follows that there is a \(k\)-algebra isomorphism

\[ \Gamma (X, U) \otimes _k \Gamma (T, V) \; \xrightarrow {\ \sim \ }\; \Gamma \bigl(X \otimes T,\ \mathfrak W(U,V)\bigr), \qquad s \otimes t \; \longmapsto \; \mathrm{fst}^\sharp (s) \cdot \mathrm{snd}^\sharp (t), \]

natural in restriction in both factors: for affine opens \(U' \subseteq U\) and \(V' \subseteq V\), restricting an identified section to \(\mathfrak W(U', V')\) equals identifying the section obtained by restricting the two tensor factors to \(U'\) and \(V'\).

Definition 317Quasi-coherence packaging on an open

Let \(X\) be a scheme, \(U\) an open of \(X\), and \(F\) a sheaf of \(k\)-modules on the small Zariski site of \(X\). A quasi-coherence packaging of \(F\) on \(U\) is the data of:

  • (P1) an action of the fixed ring \(\Gamma (X, U)\): for every open \(W \le U\) a scaling operation \(r \cdot m\) of \(r \in \Gamma (X, U)\) on \(m \in F(W)\), satisfying the module laws over \(\Gamma (X, U)\) (unit, associativity, and both distributivities) and natural under section restriction, \((r \cdot m)|_{W'} = r \cdot (m|_{W'})\) for \(W' \le W\);

  • (P2) localisation on affine opens \(V \le U\), for every \(g \in \Gamma (X, U)\), in the two-lemma form of localisation away from \(g\):

    • denominator clearing — every \(c \in F(V \cap D(g))\) is \((g^N \cdot e)|_{V \cap D(g)}\) for some \(N \ge 0\) and \(e \in F(V)\);

    • defect annihilation — every \(t \in F(V)\) with \(t|_{V \cap D(g)} = 0\) is killed by a power of \(g\): \(g^M \cdot t = 0\) for some \(M \ge 0\).

The action is by the single ring \(\Gamma (X, U)\) (not a per-open module structure), with the inclusion \(W \le U\) an explicit argument.

Definition 115Partial and rational maps

Provided by Mathlib. Let \(X, Y\) be schemes over a base \(S\). A partial map \(X \dashrightarrow Y\) is a morphism to \(Y\) from a dense open subscheme of \(X\) (its domain); a rational map is an equivalence class of partial maps, two being equivalent when they agree on a common dense open. For \(X\) irreducible with generic point \(\xi \) and function field \(K(X) = \mathcal{O}_{X,\xi }\), a partial map \(g\) restricts to a morphism \(\operatorname{Spec}K(X) \to Y\) (its function-field morphism), which determines the rational map. For \(X\) integral and \(Y\) locally of finite type over \(S\):

  1. every \(S\)-morphism \(\operatorname{Spec}K(X) \to Y\) arises as the function-field morphism of a unique rational \(S\)-map \(X \dashrightarrow Y\) (spreading out);

  2. if moreover an \(S\)-morphism \(\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal{O}_{X,x} \to Y\) restricting to the given one on \(\operatorname{Spec}K(X)\) exists at a point \(x\), then \(x\) lies in the domain of definition of that rational map (the union of the domains of its representatives);

  3. if \(Y\) is separated, a rational map has a largest representative, defined on its whole domain of definition.

Definition 683The relative Picard group

kleiman-picard Let \(C\) be an object of \(\mathrm{Over}(\operatorname{Spec}k)\) and \(T\) a test object. Write \(H_T \le \operatorname{Pic}(C \otimes T)\) for the subgroup of Čech Picard classes pulled back from the base: the range of \(\mathrm{pr}_2^{*} = \mathrm{snd}^{*} \colon \operatorname{Pic}(T) \to \operatorname{Pic}(C \otimes T)\), so \(L \in H_T\) iff \(L = \mathrm{snd}^{*} N\) for some \(N \in \operatorname{Pic}(T)\). The relative Picard group is the quotient

\[ \mathrm{relPic}(C,T) \; :=\; \operatorname{Pic}(C \otimes T) \, /\, H_T , \]

a commutative group, with surjective projection \(\pi _T \colon \operatorname{Pic}(C \otimes T) \to \mathrm{relPic}(C,T)\). The exact coset relation holds: \(\pi _T L = \pi _T L'\) iff \(L / L' \in H_T\) — a genuine range condition, involving no choice.

Definition 748Transport family

A transport family from \(D\) to \(E\) assigns to every test algebra \(B\) a morphism

\[ h_B \colon D \otimes \operatorname{Spec}B \longrightarrow E \otimes \operatorname{Spec}B \]

of the underlying schemes of the two product bundles (the product on the left taken over \(\operatorname{Spec}k_D\), on the right over \(\operatorname{Spec}k_E\)), such that:

  1. (projection compatibility) \(\mathrm{snd}_E \circ h_B = \mathrm{snd}_D\) as morphisms to the shared scheme \(\operatorname{Spec}B\);

  2. (naturality) for every homomorphism \(f \colon B \to B'\) of test algebras that is simultaneously \(k_D\)-linear and \(k_E\)-linear, \((E \lhd \operatorname{Spec}f) \circ h_{B'} = h_B \circ (D \lhd \operatorname{Spec}f)\) as morphisms \(D \otimes \operatorname{Spec}B' \to E \otimes \operatorname{Spec}B\).

Definition 511The skyscraper sheaf of \(K\)-modules

Definition 450The two-cover pair data of a packaged sheaf

Definition 417Two-lattice pair

A two-lattice pair \(P\) over \(R\) consists of:

  • \(R\)-modules \(M_0\), \(M_1\) (the chart lattices) and \(N\) (the overlap module);

  • \(R\)-linear endomorphisms \(t_0\) of \(M_0\) and \(t_1\) of \(M_1\) (the coordinate actions) and an invertible \(R\)-linear endomorphism \(u\) of \(N\);

  • \(R\)-linear maps \(\iota _0 : M_0 \to N\) and \(\iota _1 : M_1 \to N\) (the restrictions to the overlap) intertwining the actions: \(\iota _0(t_0 x) = u(\iota _0 x)\) for all \(x \in M_0\) and \(\iota _1(t_1 y) = u^{-1}(\iota _1 y)\) for all \(y \in M_1\);

subject to the localization axioms:

  1. denominator clearing: every \(n \in N\) admits an integer \(m \ge 0\) and \(x \in M_0\) with \(u^m n = \iota _0 x\), and an integer \(m' \ge 0\) and \(y \in M_1\) with \(u^{-m'} n = \iota _1 y\);

  2. annihilation: if \(\iota _0 x = 0\) then \(t_0^m x = 0\) for some \(m \ge 0\), and if \(\iota _1 y = 0\) then \(t_1^m y = 0\) for some \(m \ge 0\).

Regarding \(M_0\) and \(N\) as modules over the polynomial ring \(R[t]\), with \(t\) acting as \(t_0\) on \(M_0\) and as \(u\) on \(N\), the three conditions — invertibility of \(u\) on \(N\), clearing, annihilation — say precisely that \(\iota _0\) exhibits \(N\) as the localization of \(M_0\) at the powers of \(t\); likewise \(\iota _1\) exhibits \(N\) as the localization of \(M_1\) at the powers of \(t\), for the structures through \(t_1\) and \(u^{-1}\). In the geometric application \(M_0, M_1\) are the sections of a quasi-coherent sheaf on the two charts of an affine two-cover, \(N\) its sections on the overlap, and \(t_0, t_1\) the two chart coordinates, mutually inverse on the overlap.

Lemma 333Contravariant long exact sequence of \(\operatorname{Ext}\)

Provided by Mathlib. Let \(0 \to A \xrightarrow {f} B \xrightarrow {g} C \to 0\) be a short exact sequence in an abelian category with \(\operatorname{Ext}\)-groups and let \(Y\) be any object. There is a canonical extension class \(\delta \in \operatorname{Ext}^1(C, A)\) (built from the connecting homomorphism of the sequence), and for every \(n \ge 0\) the sequence of abelian groups

\[ \operatorname{Ext}^n(C,Y) \xrightarrow {g^*} \operatorname{Ext}^n(B,Y) \xrightarrow {f^*} \operatorname{Ext}^n(A,Y) \xrightarrow {\ \delta \cdot (-)\ } \operatorname{Ext}^{n+1}(C,Y) \xrightarrow {g^*} \operatorname{Ext}^{n+1}(B,Y) \xrightarrow {f^*} \operatorname{Ext}^{n+1}(A,Y) \]

is exact at each of the four inner terms, where \(f^*, g^*\) are precomposition (contravariant functoriality of \(\operatorname{Ext}(-,Y)\)) and \(\delta \cdot (-)\) is composition (Yoneda product) with \(\delta \). (Convention: \(\operatorname{Ext}^0 = \operatorname{Hom}\).) If \(B = X_2 \oplus X_3\) is a direct sum, \(\operatorname{Ext}^n(B,Y) \cong \operatorname{Ext}^n(X_2,Y) \times \operatorname{Ext}^n(X_3,Y)\) naturally, compatibly with \(f^*, g^*\).

Lemma 260The covariant long exact sequence of \(\operatorname{Ext}\)

Provided by Mathlib. Let \(0 \to A \xrightarrow {f} B \xrightarrow {g} C \to 0\) be a short exact sequence in an abelian category with \(\operatorname{Ext}\)-groups, with extension class \(\delta \in \operatorname{Ext}^1(C, A)\) (333), and let \(Y\) be any object. For every \(n \geq 0\) the sequence of abelian groups

\[ \operatorname{Ext}^n(Y, A) \xrightarrow {f_*} \operatorname{Ext}^n(Y, B) \xrightarrow {g_*} \operatorname{Ext}^n(Y, C) \xrightarrow {(-) \cdot \delta } \operatorname{Ext}^{n+1}(Y, A) \xrightarrow {f_*} \operatorname{Ext}^{n+1}(Y, B) \]

is exact at each inner term, where \(f_*, g_*\) are postcomposition (covariant functoriality of \(\operatorname{Ext}(Y, -)\)) and \((-) \cdot \delta \) is the Yoneda product with the extension class. Moreover, if \(f : A \to B\) is a monomorphism then postcomposition \(f_* : \operatorname{Ext}^0(Y, A) \to \operatorname{Ext}^0(Y, B)\) is injective (in degree zero \(\operatorname{Ext}^0 = \operatorname{Hom}\), and postcomposition with a mono is injective on \(\operatorname{Hom}\)).

\[ f^{(1)}_x\big|_{\mathcal W(x)} \; =\; u_x \cdot f^{(2)}_x\big|_{\mathcal W(x)}, \qquad u_x \in \mathcal{O}_{X}(\mathcal W(x))^{\times }. \]

Lemma 1088The amalgamation seam and the compatibility descent

Let \(F\) be a presheaf on \(\mathrm{Over}(S)\) and \(\widetilde F\) its \(\Sigma \)-extension.

  1. (Amalgamation seam) For \(g \colon T' \to T\), \(a \colon T \to S\), \(b \colon T' \to S\) with \(g \circ a = b\), and elements \(s \in F(T,a)\), \(y \in F(T',b)\): \(g^{*}\langle a, s\rangle = \langle b, y\rangle \) in \(\widetilde F(T')\) iff \(s\) restricts to \(y\) along the slice morphism \((T',b) \to (T,a)\) induced by \(g\).

  2. (Left-leg rule) For a slice morphism \(g \colon Z \to (T,a)\) and \(x \in F(T,a)\): restriction of \(\langle a, x\rangle \) along the underlying map of \(g\) is \(\langle Z_{\mathrm{struct}},\, F(g)^{*}x \rangle \), the honest slice restriction on the fibre.

  3. (Compatibility descent) If two \(\Sigma \)-elements \(\langle a, x\rangle , \langle b, y\rangle \) have equal restrictions along the underlying maps of a pair of slice morphisms \(g_a \colon Z \to (T,a)\), \(g_b \colon Z' = Z \to (T',b)\), then \(F(g_a)^{*}x = F(g_b)^{*}y\).

Lemma 819Pullback of a coboundary relation

Let \(\varphi \colon X \to Y\), \(r_1 \colon Y \to Z_1\), \(r_2 \colon Y \to Z_2\). Suppose a unit \(0\)-cochain \(c\) on a pointed cover \(\mathcal C\) of \(Y\) cobounds the comparison of two pair-indexed unit families \(E_1\) on \(Z_1\) and \(E_2\) on \(Z_2\), pulled back along \(r_1\) and \(r_2\): for all \(y, y' \in Y\), on the overlap \(\mathcal C(y) \cap \mathcal C(y')\),

\[ c_y \cdot \bigl(r_1^{\sharp } E_1\bigr)_{y y'} = \bigl(r_2^{\sharp } E_2\bigr)_{y y'} \cdot c_{y'} . \]

Then for every \(x, x' \in X\) and every open \(O \subseteq \varphi ^{-1}(\mathcal C(\varphi x) \cap \mathcal C(\varphi x'))\), the pullback of the relation along \(\varphi \) holds in composite normal form:

\[ \varphi ^{\sharp }_O\, c_{\varphi x} \cdot \bigl((r_1\varphi )^{\sharp }_O E_1\bigr)_{x x'} = \bigl((r_2\varphi )^{\sharp }_O E_2\bigr)_{x x'} \cdot \varphi ^{\sharp }_O\, c_{\varphi x'}, \]

where \(r_i\varphi \) denotes the composite \(X \xrightarrow {\varphi } Y \xrightarrow {r_i} Z_i\).

Theorem 135The lift-app rule

Let \(U\), \(V\) be affine and let \(q \colon Z \to X \otimes T\) be a morphism of \(\mathrm{Over}(\operatorname{Spec}k)\) with components \(a := \mathrm{fst} \circ q \colon Z \to X\) and \(b := \mathrm{snd} \circ q \colon Z \to T\). Then on any open \(W\) of \(Z\) contained in \(q^{-1}\mathfrak W(U,V)\), in \(a^{-1}(U)\) and in \(b^{-1}(V)\), the pullback \(q^\sharp \) sends the identified pure tensor and its difference shape to

\[ q^\sharp \bigl(s \otimes t\bigr) = a^\sharp (s) \cdot b^\sharp (t), \qquad q^\sharp \bigl(s \otimes 1 - 1 \otimes t\bigr) = a^\sharp (s) - b^\sharp (t). \]

In particular, for the morphism \(\langle a, b\rangle \colon Z \to X \otimes T\) into the product determined by two maps \(a \colon Z \to X\), \(b \colon Z \to T\), the pullback \(\langle a, b\rangle ^\sharp \) sends \(s \otimes t\) to \(a^\sharp (s) \cdot b^\sharp (t)\).

Theorem 967Triviality detection for the affine-open class

Let \(Z\) be a scheme and \(L\) a Čech Picard class on \(Z\).

  1. If the affine-open class \(L\langle O\rangle \) is trivial for an affine open \(O\), then the restriction \(\iota ^{*}L\) of \(L\) to \(O\) is trivial.

  2. Restriction triviality is monotone: if \(\iota _O^{*}L = 1\) and \(O' \le O\), then \(\iota _{O'}^{*}L = 1\).

  3. If, for an affine open \(O\) and \(f \in \Gamma (Z, O)\), the invertible module \(L\langle O\rangle \) becomes free over every \(\Gamma (Z, O)\)-algebra in which \(f\) is a unit, then the affine-open class on the basic open \(D(f)\) is trivial, \(L\langle D(f)\rangle = 1\); hence \(L\) restricts trivially to \(D(f)\).

Theorem 1017The kernel is the principal divisors

Two Weil divisors have the same Čech Picard class if and only if they differ by a principal divisor:

\[ \mathcal{O}_{X}(D) = \mathcal{O}_{X}(D') \iff D - D' = \mathrm{div}(g) \text{ for some } g \in K(X)^{\times }. \]

Together with surjectivity (1015) this identifies \(\operatorname{Pic}(X)\) with the group of Weil divisors modulo principal divisors, the classical isomorphism \(\mathrm{CaCl}(X) = \operatorname{Pic}(X)\) on an integral curve.

Theorem 1124The auxiliary fixed-window universal family — unproved

There exists an affine pullback package for \(\mathbf{Div}\) in the sense of 1122; equivalently, there is a compatible chart family — a certified divisor family \(U_{ij}\) of degree \(g\) over the coordinate ring of each affine chart of \(\mathbf{Div}\), whose window pair is the tautological pair of that chart, and whose pullbacks along two presentations of one morphism agree in \(\operatorname{Div}^{\, g}_{\mathrm{Zar}}\).

This statement is not proved. It is the forward direction of representability: given a point \((K_1, K_2)\) of \(\mathbf{Div}\) over \(R\), one must produce the divisor whose windows are \(K_1\) and \(K_2\). The intended construction takes a generating family of \(K_1\) inside \(R \otimes _k H_M\) and reads its common vanishing locus as an effective divisor, with local equations extracted chart by chart; the two obstacles are that this produces the local equations only after a Zariski localisation of \(R\) — which is why the target is \(\operatorname{Div}^{\, g}_{\mathrm{Zar}}\) and not \(\operatorname{Div}^{\, g}\), and why the global certificate of 1106 is unavailable (1108) — and that the resulting family’s second window must be shown to be exactly \(K_2\), for which the containment \(K_2 \subseteq K_{M+s}\) has to be upgraded from the fibrewise statement to a relative one, an upgrade that fails over nonreduced base rings if attempted fibrewise.

Everything in Sections 8.2–8.5 is independent of this statement. This is a conditional result for the pinned-window auxiliary carrier, not the current R2 representability target \(\operatorname {divFunctorAff}(C,n)\).

Theorem 643The order table of the fibre unit

Theorem 1108The chart obstruction to a global certificate

is a pullback of schemes; here the top edge is the first slice projection \(\mathrm{fst} : (f^{*}X \otimes T)_{\mathrm{left}} \to (f^{*}X)_{\mathrm{left}} = X_{\mathrm{left}} \times _S S'\) followed by the first projection of the fibre product, and the bottom edge \(f \circ T.\mathrm{hom}\) is the structure morphism of \(f_{!}T\). Theorem 325The packaging axioms are the localisation axioms

Let \(U\) be an affine open of a scheme \(X\), let \(F\) be a sheaf of \(k\)-modules with a quasi-coherence packaging on \(U\), and let \(g \in \Gamma (X, U)\) act invertibly on \(F(U \cap D(g))\) (for the module structure of 323).   1. every element of \(S\) acts invertibly on \(F(U \cap D(g))\);

  2. every \(c \in F(U \cap D(g))\) is of the form \(g^{-N} \cdot (e|_{U \cap D(g)})\) for some \(N \ge 0\) and \(e \in F(U)\);

  3. any two sections of \(F(U)\) with equal restriction to \(U \cap D(g)\) differ by an element killed by a power of \(g\).

These three properties characterise the localisation map \(M \to S^{-1}M\) up to unique isomorphism under \(F(U)\).

Theorem 80Structure theorem for standard smooth algebras

stacks-project Provided by Mathlib. Let \(R\) be a commutative ring and \(S\) an \(R\)-algebra which is standard smooth of relative dimension \(n\): it admits a presentation \(S = R[x_1,\dots ,x_m]/(f_1,\dots ,f_c)\) with \(m - c = n\) in which the Jacobian matrix \((\partial f_u/\partial x_v)_{u,v \le c}\) has invertible determinant in \(S\). Then the structure map factors as

\[ R \longrightarrow R[y_1, \dots , y_n] \longrightarrow S \]

with the second homomorphism étale. (For such a presentation the module of Kähler differentials \(\Omega _{S/R}\) is free on the images of \(dx_{c+1}, \dots , dx_m\); consequently \(S\) is unramified, hence étale, over the polynomial subring on those last \(n\) coordinates.)

Theorem 613The fiber-degree identity

Let \(V\) be an affine chart of \(C_{K_1}\) containing the generic point, let \(t \in \Gamma (C_{K_1}, V)\) be a section whose germ at \(\eta \) is the value of a unit \(g \in K(C_{K_1})^{\times }\) and which is a unit at every point of \(V\) other than a fixed non-generic point \(x' \in V\), and let \(S\) be a finite set of non-generic points of \(C_{K_2}\), contained in \(\pi ^{-1}V\), outside which the pulled-back section \(\pi ^{\sharp }t\) is a unit on \(\pi ^{-1}V\). Then, in \(\mathbb {Z}\),

\[ \sum _{x'' \in S} \mathrm{ord}_{x''}\bigl(\pi ^{\sharp }g\bigr) \cdot \bigl[\kappa (x'') : K_2\bigr] \; =\; \mathrm{ord}_{x'}(g) \cdot \bigl[\kappa (x') : K_1\bigr]. \]

(Mathematically, the left side is the sum over the fibre of \(x'\): the hypotheses force \(S\) to exhaust the non-unit locus of \(\pi ^{\sharp }t\) on the chart, which is contained in \(\pi ^{-1}(x')\) since unit germs pull back to unit germs; points of \(S\) outside that locus contribute order zero. The statement is parameterised by such a finite \(S\) exactly so that the consumer may take for \(S\) the support of a divisor already in hand.)

Theorem 634The fiber-degree identity for a finite morphism

hartshorne-algebraic-geometry:page-0155 Let \(K\) be a field, \(X\) and \(Y\) integral schemes smooth of relative dimension one over \(\operatorname{Spec}K\), and \(f : X \to Y\) a finite morphism over \(\operatorname{Spec}K\) with \(f(\eta _X) = \eta _Y\). Let \(V \ni \eta _Y\) be an affine chart of \(Y\), let \(t \in \Gamma (Y, V)\) be a section whose germ at \(\eta _Y\) is the value of a unit \(g \in K(Y)^{\times }\), let \(y \in V\) be a non-generic point with \(\mathrm{ord}_y(g) = 1\) at which the tracked section is normalized, \(t\) being a unit at every point of \(V\) other than \(y\); and let \(S\) be a finite set of non-generic points of \(X\), contained in \(f^{-1}V\), outside which the pulled section \(f^{\sharp }t\) is a unit on \(f^{-1}V\). Then, in \(\mathbb {Z}\),

\[ \sum _{z \in S} \mathrm{ord}_z\bigl(f^{\sharp }g\bigr) \cdot \bigl[\kappa (z) : K\bigr] \; =\; \bigl[K(X) : K(Y)\bigr] \cdot \bigl[\kappa (y) : K\bigr]. \]

(The hypotheses force \(S\) to exhaust the non-unit locus of \(f^{\sharp }t\), which is contained in the fiber \(f^{-1}(y)\); members of \(S\) outside that locus contribute order zero. The statement is parameterised by such a finite \(S\) so that the consumer may take for \(S\) the support of a divisor already in hand.)

Theorem 180Two-lattice finiteness, spanning-set form

hartshorne-algebraic-geometry:page-0242, hartshorne-algebraic-geometry:page-0243 Let \(k\) be a commutative ring and \(N\) a module over \(k[T,T^{-1}]\) whose \(k\)-module structure is the restriction of scalars of the \(k[T,T^{-1}]\)-action along the canonical ring map \(k \to k[T,T^{-1}]\). Let \(Q_0, Q_1 \subseteq N\) be \(k\)-submodules and \(s \subset N\) a finite subset such that:

  1. \(s \subseteq Q_0\);

  2. \(s\) spans \(N\) over \(k[T,T^{-1}]\): \(\langle s \rangle _{k[T,T^{-1}]} = N\);

  3. \(Q_0\) is stable under multiplication by \(T\): \(T \cdot x \in Q_0\) for all \(x \in Q_0\);

  4. \(Q_1\) is stable under multiplication by \(T^{-1}\): \(T^{-1} \cdot x \in Q_1\) for all \(x \in Q_1\);

  5. every \(n \in N\) is eventually absorbed by \(Q_1\): there is an integer \(m \ge 0\) with \(T^{-m} \cdot n \in Q_1\).

Then \(N / (Q_0 + Q_1)\) is a finite \(k\)-module: it is spanned by the classes of the monomials \(T^j \cdot x\), for \(x \in s\) and \(-M {\lt} j {\lt} 0\), where \(M\) is any uniform bound with \(T^{-M} \cdot x \in Q_1\) for every \(x \in s\).

stacks-project Let \(k\) be a commutative ring, \(X\) a scheme over \(\operatorname{Spec}k\), and \(U_0, U_1\) affine opens of \(X\) with \(U_0 \cup U_1 = X\). There is a \(k\)-linear isomorphism

Theorem 454The rigid engine, sheaf level

kleiman-picard Let \(R\) be Noetherian, \(U_0, U_1\) affine opens covering \(X\), and \(d\) two-cover pair data for the packaged sheaf \(F\) whose pair \(P\) has finite lattices (the chart sections \(F(U_i)\) are finite over \(R[t]\) through the coordinate actions). Assume the section modules are tame: \(F(U_0) \times F(U_1)\) is a flat \(R\)-module and \(F(U_0 \cap U_1)\) is a projective \(R\)-module (in the intended applications all three are free). If every residue-field fibre of \(H^1\) of the pair vanishes,

\[ H^1(P) \otimes _R \kappa (\mathfrak p) = 0 \quad \text{for every prime } \mathfrak p \subseteq R, \]

then

\[ H^1(X, F) = 0, \qquad \text{and } H^0(X, F) \text{ is a finite projective } R\text{-module}. \]

This is the curve-lite form of Kleiman’s criterion for the module \(\mathcal Q\): vanishing of the degree-one cohomology of the fibres ((v) of the source) forces the representing module to be free/projective ((i)) — here delivered on a two-chart cover with the two-term Čech complex playing the role of the pushforward. The fibre hypothesis is deliberately consumed in this complex form (fibres of \(H^1\) of the pair); its sheaf-level discharge — identifying the fibre of the complex with the cohomology of a fibre sheaf — is a seam of a later campaign and is not part of this statement.

Let \(\varphi \colon X' \to Y\) and let \(O \subseteq X'\) be an open inside \(\varphi ^{-1}(\mathcal C_{\varphi x} \cap D)\). Then the \(\varphi \)-pullback of a glued corrected unit \(u\) expands into its three factors, the correction factors pulled back along the composites \(\varphi \circ r_1\) and \(\varphi \circ r_2\):

\[ \varphi ^{\sharp } u = (\varphi r_1)^{\sharp }\gamma _Z(a,\, (\varphi r_1)x) \cdot \bigl(\varphi ^{\sharp } c_{\varphi x}\bigr)^{-1} \cdot (\varphi r_2)^{\sharp }\gamma _Z((\varphi r_2)x,\, b) . \]

Theorem 927Rigidity of automorphisms of a rigidified pair

kleiman-picard Let the curve \(C\) be proper, geometrically irreducible and geometrically reduced. For every point \(\sigma \colon \operatorname{Spec}A \to C\), pullback of global unit sections along the section of the projection,

\[ g_\sigma ^{\sharp } \colon \Gamma (\operatorname{Spec}A, \top )^{\times } \; \longrightarrow \; \Gamma (X_A, \top )^{\times }, \]

is a bijection. In particular, a global unit of the curve \(X_A\) whose restriction along the section is \(1\) is itself \(1\). This is the cocycle form of Kleiman’s automorphism rigidity: an automorphism of a rigidified pair is trivial.

Assume the witness relation for \(c\): on the overlaps of \(\mathcal C\), \(c_x \cdot r_1^{\sharp }\gamma _Z(r_1 x, r_1 y) = r_2^{\sharp }\gamma _Z(r_2 x, r_2 y) \cdot c_y\). Theorem 801Naturality of the descent equivalence in the test object

Let \(g \colon T' \to T\) be a morphism of test objects and \(V \subseteq T_{\mathrm{left}}\) an affine open whose preimage \(g_{\mathrm{left}}^{-1} V \subseteq T'_{\mathrm{left}}\) is also affine. For \(v \in \Gamma (T_{\mathrm{left}}, V)^{\times }\), descending \(v\) on \(T\) and then pulling back along \(C \lhd g\) equals first pulling \(v\) back along \(g\) and then descending on \(T'\); both are units over \(\mathrm{pr}'^{-1}(g_{\mathrm{left}}^{-1} V)\).

Theorem 817Naturality of the top-open descent

For a \(k\)-algebra homomorphism \(\varphi \colon R \to R'\), descending a global unit on \(\operatorname{Spec}R\) and pulling it back along \(C \lhd \operatorname{Spec}\varphi \) equals first pulling back along \(\operatorname{Spec}\varphi \) and then descending on \(\operatorname{Spec}R'\).

Theorem 76Unramified finite-type domains over a Dedekind domain, DVR form

Let \(A\) be a Dedekind domain and \(B\) an integral domain which is an \(A\)-algebra of finite type and formally unramified over \(A\). Then \(B\) is Noetherian, and the localization of \(B\) at every nonzero prime ideal is a discrete valuation ring.

Theorem 852The Amitsur cocycle identity of the glued components

Over the triple basic open of \(\operatorname{Spec}(B \otimes _A (B \otimes _A B))\), the coface pullbacks of the glued witness components satisfy the Amitsur cocycle identity:

\[ f_{23}^{\sharp }\, \mathrm{witnessBasicSection}(j, l) \cdot f_{12}^{\sharp }\, \mathrm{witnessBasicSection}(i, j) = f_{13}^{\sharp }\, \mathrm{witnessBasicSection}(i, l) . \]

Theorem 853The diagonal collapse of the glued components

The \(\Delta \)-pullback of the glued witness component onto the Zariski overlap \(D(P.r_i \cdot P.r_j) \subseteq \operatorname{Spec}B\) is the Zariski cover cocycle value \(\gamma _{ij}\) of \(P\):

\[ \Delta ^{\sharp }\, \mathrm{witnessBasicSection}(i, j) = \gamma _{ij} . \]

Theorem 1299The Yoneda embedding for group objects

Let \(\mathcal C\) be a cartesian monoidal category. Sending a group object \(G\) to the presheaf of groups \(\operatorname{Hom}(-, G)\) is a fully faithful embedding of the category of group objects of \(\mathcal C\) into presheaves of groups on \(\mathcal C\). If a presheaf of groups \(F\) is representable, with representing object \(J\), then the transported group structure makes \(J\) a group object and \(\operatorname{Hom}(-, J) \cong F\) as presheaves of groups.

Theorem 1243The zero locus of a regular function is pure codimension one

abelian-varieties:page-0024 Let \(X\) be an integral, locally Noetherian scheme with regular stalks. Let \(P \in X\) and let \(s \in \mathcal{O}_{X,P}\) lie in the maximal ideal, with nonzero image \(t \in K(X)\).
